newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Demand spurs Nigerian share trading.
newsitem.headline: Demand spurs Nigerian share trading.

text.p: Shares of Nigerian blue chips rose steadily in Tuesday's trade at the Nigerian stock market, buoyed by insatiable demand.
The all-share index closed at 8508.86 from 8450.84 on Monday on the back of increasing demand for banks, conglomerates, food and beverages shares, traders said.
"There was plenty of action, particularly in conglomerates, because of good prospects and major banks because of government directive that they should recapitalise," said one trader.
UAC shot up by 70 kobo, about five percent, to 15.20 naira on positive prospects while PZ Industries PZIN.LG rose 30 kobo to 26.00 naira.
Lever Brothers ended 50 kobo up at 25.90 naira.
First Bank continued to soar, ending 25 kobo stronger at 18.50 naira in anticipation of an improved full year result, dealers said.
"Besides the current buying of bank shares to benefit from their capital appreciation, the market is expecting First Bank to post a better result than the others," one said.
Union Bank and UBA each rose 10 kobo to 15.60 naira and 13.50 naira, respectively.

West African Portland Cement Company and Nigerian Breweries remained among favourites of investors. The cement firm closed 30 kobo up at 63.50 naira while the brewer ended 20 kobo higher at 19.25 naira.
The usually buoyant petroleum shares remained quiet on Tuesday because of a week-long fuel scarcity, traders said.
Tuesday's main loser Benue Cement fell 14 kobo to 5.45 naira because investors were selling large amounts.
Lack of interest saw Chemical and Allied Products slide one kobo to 4.39 naira.
